Sixteen teams competed in the league – the top twelve teams from the previous season, the two play-off winners and two teams promoted from the [[2017–18 Prince Mohammad bin Salman League]]. '''Teams who were promoted to the Pro League''' The first club to be promoted was [[Al Wehda FC|Al-Wehda]], following their 2–2 draw away to [[Al-Mujazzal Club|Al-Mujazzal]] on 11 April 2018. Al-Wehda will play in the top flight of Saudi football after a season absence.{{Cite news |title=بتعادل مع المجزل.. الوحدة يعود لدوري المحترفين|url=http://www.kooora.com/?n=691686|publisher=kooora|date=11 April 2018 |access-date=21 April 2018}} They were crowned champions on 18 April 2018 after beating [[Al-Khaleej FC|Al-Khaleej]] 1–0 at home.{{Cite news |title= ألف مبروك لنادي #الوحدة تتويجه بلقب #دوري_الأمير_محمد_بن_سلمان |url=https://twitter.com/saudiFF/status/986690786711531522|publisher=saff|date=18 April 2018 |access-date=21 April 2018}} The second club to be promoted was [[Al-Hazem F.C.|Al-Hazem]], following their 4–1 win at home against [[Al-Mujazzal Club|Al-Mujazzal]] on 18 April 2017, coupled with [[Al-Tai FC|Al-Tai's]] defeat against [[Hajer FC|Hajer]]. Al-Hazem will play in the top flight of Saudi football for the first time since 2010–11.{{Cite news |title= ألف مبروك لنادي #الحزم صعوده لـ #الدوري_السعودي_للمحترفين|url=https://twitter.com/saudiFF/status/986690963044208641|publisher=saff|date=18 April 2018 |access-date=21 April 2018}} '''Teams who were relegated to the MS League''' No teams were relegated to the Prince Mohammad bin Salman League. Due to an increase in the number of teams, the Saudi FF announced that the relegation was canceled and in its place was a relegation play-off.
